abstract: This paper describes a competition system for the 5th ETRI Human Understanding AI Paper Challenge. The task is to predict seven binary daily targets spanning subjective sleep quality, fatigue, stress, and objective sleep-health guideline adherence from multimodal lifelog data. The confirmed public anchor of the system is ID342, a conservative feature-similarity shrink blend between a known public anchor lineage and an independent feature-similarity source. The workflow prioritizes leaderboard transfer safety over local cross-validation gains: candidate promotion is blocked unless a model improves local validation while also surviving stable-shape, failed-frontier, and public-gap risk checks. The best confirmed public score as of 2026-06-25 is 0.5960832519. Extensive late-stage audits found that weather, AirKorea pollution context, historical ETRI survey/sleep priors, raw temporal representations, missingness-aware subject-state embeddings, and registered material-source recombinations did not open a credible Public 0.58 review path. The resulting system is best characterized as a robust anchor-controlled ensemble with explicit negative-evidence accounting rather than an overfit local-frontier solution.
title: Conservative Multimodal Lifelog Modeling with Public-Anchor Risk Control for Sleep and Stress State Prediction
